haiku-low.q1: Both return the same HTTP 401 login page with "Invalid email or password" and run the same statements, including one bcrypt verify (dummy hash for unknown emails).
haiku-low.q2: It gets HTTP 429 with Retry-After and no password check, for 15 minutes from the lock. Refused attempts are not recorded.
haiku-low.q3: On successful login, the cookie's old session is destroyed and a new random session ID is issued. A failed login leaves the existing session unchanged.
haiku-low.q4: Only an opaque random session ID, in a cookie named sid with HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Lax. Page scripts cannot read it because of HttpOnly.
haiku-low.q5: It stops working 12 hours after login. Expires_at is fixed at creation, and each request refreshes only the 30-minute idle clock, so constant use does not extend it.
haiku-low.q6: It clears the cookie (Max-Age 0) and redirects with 303 to /login. Expired or idle sessions are treated the same way.
haiku-low.q7: The server deletes the session row before replying, then clears the cookie and redirects to /login. If the session is already gone, the same response is returned.
haiku-low.q8: In Postgres, shared by both instances. Any instance finds it by looking up the SHA-256 hash of the cookie value in the sessions table.
haiku-low.q9: In the login_failures table, one row per failure with email and time. The count takes rows at or after now minus 10 minutes, inclusive, so the window slides.
haiku-low.q10: It compares the sid hash and requires last_seen_at within 30 minutes and expires_at in the future. On success it writes last_seen_at = now().
haiku-low.q11: HTTP 503 with "Sign-in is temporarily unavailable. Try again shortly." The transaction rolls back, and the old session cookie is kept if present.
haiku-low.q12: A sweeper runs every 10 minutes on each instance, deleting rejected sessions in batches of up to 1000. Rejected rows are never accepted, even before deletion.

sonnet.q1: It doesn't differ. Both get HTTP 401 with the login page and "Invalid email or password" (byte-identical body, same statements run, one bcrypt verify against a dummy hash for unknown email).
sonnet.q2: It is refused with HTTP 429 (login page, Retry-After in seconds) without checking the password. The lock lasts 15 minutes from when the fifth failure was recorded, and refused attempts are not recorded.
sonnet.q3: On success, the old session (found by hashing the incoming sid) is deleted in the same transaction and a new random session ID is issued. The browser gets a 303 to /dashboard and a new sid cookie. On a failed login (401/429/503) the existing session is kept.
sonnet.q4: Only the opaque session ID: a random 32-byte token, base64url-encoded. It is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it. It is also Secure, SameSite=Lax and Path=/.
sonnet.q5: 12 hours after login, because expires_at = created_at + 12 hours is fixed and never extended. Each request restarts the 30-minute idle clock but not the 12-hour limit.
sonnet.q6: The touch UPDATE returns no row. The server responds 303 to /login with Set-Cookie sid Max-Age=0 (same attributes), which clears the cookie. It does not delete the row, because the request path never deletes.
sonnet.q7: With a cookie, the server runs DELETE on sessions where id_hash is the hash of the sid before replying. The reply is 303 to /login with the cookie cleared (Max-Age 0). If the session is already gone, the DELETE affects 0 rows and still succeeds, so the response is the same. With no cookie, there is no database access and the cookie is cleared. If the DELETE fails, the reply is 503 and the cookie is kept.
sonnet.q8: In the shared Postgres database, in the sessions table keyed by the SHA-256 hash of the cookie value (id_hash). Both app instances read and write the same tables. An instance hashes the sid from the cookie and looks up that row.
sonnet.q9: In the Postgres table login_failures, one row per failure (email, failed_at), with locks in login_locks. A failure counts if failed_at >= now_ts - 10 minutes, where now_ts is the database clock_timestamp() read after taking the advisory lock. The window is inclusive and sliding.
sonnet.q10: It runs one UPDATE that checks last_seen_at > now() - 30 minutes and expires_at > now(), using the database clock. When the row matches, it writes last_seen_at = now() and returns user_id.
sonnet.q11: HTTP 503 with "Sign-in is temporarily unavailable. Try again shortly." The transaction is rolled back, so failures and locks are not cleared. The cookie is unchanged, so any existing session is kept. If the COMMIT outcome is unknown, the old session may be deleted and no new one created.
sonnet.q12: A sweeper that runs on every app instance every 10 minutes, with a random initial offset. It deletes in batches of 1000 the sessions where expires_at <= now() or last_seen_at <= now() - 30 minutes. The request path never deletes.
